title: Added feature to restart profiler after it has been stopped.
body:
To address #17, I changed it so that the "stop profiling" button changes to a "restart profiling" button after it is pressed.

This is done by saving the slot reference and using it to rerun the initialization script when the user presses the button for a second time. In order to avoid conflicts, some extra disposal code has been added to the panel initializer. 

Effectively, this just deletes everything and re-creates it when the user presses the "restart profiler" button. While not the most elegant way of handling this functionality, it is a handy shortcut for deleting the profiler and spawning another in, which is all it needs to be.

*This PR is not quite ready yet. I still have to fix a crash that happens when opening two profilers and trying to profile at the same time*
author: AwesomeTornado

comments.body:
Alright, I have added a quick feature that only allows a single "active" profiler that can be started and stopped at a time. 

I should note that I was unable to reproduce my original crash, so it might be ok to remove this restriction, however that would then require a couple scoping issues to be solved. (Pressing the "restart" button on an old profiler would restart the most recently spawned profiler)
Also, I have not tested this in a world with more than one user (myself) in it yet.

This should be ok to merge.
Found a couple bugs, apologies for the back and forth on whether this is ready to merge. I’m doing more thorough testing now, will update this soon.

Ok, I did a bit more work on it and think that I have fixed the problem.

I have tested all of the basic features:
 - opening two inspectors at the same time
 - restarting inspectors
 - closing inspectors without stopping them
 - creating new inspectors without stopping old ones
 - spamming the "restart profiler" button

 and whatever else I could think of.

This was all tested on a headless, in my localhome, and in a self hosted world. I tried it for a short period with one other person in the world, and it seemed to be fine.

After not noticing the problems with my previous version, I would greatly appreciate it if you (Esnya) or @Stellanora64 could try it out a bit to make sure there are no issues, and let me know if there are things that I should change.

title: Feature request: ability to re-enable profiling after stopping it
body: Currently when the profiler is stopped there is no way to start profiling again without making a new metrics profiler. This isn't a major issue but can be tedious when profiling worlds to see if changes to the world are having an affect to performance.
author: Stellanora64

comments.body:
Thank you for the feature request!

When profiling is re-enabled:
- If previous data is retained:
  - Old and new metrics combine, reducing measurement accuracy.
- If metrics are reset:
  - The result is effectively the same as opening a new profiler, but with fewer steps.

In my view, using new profiler windows provides clearer comparisons and remains the better approach.

Due to current design constraints, re-enabling profiling is challenging, but we may revisit this idea in the future if the need grows.

I think the way of restarting the profiler from scratch would at least be helpful in my use case (like a refresh button next to stop profiling), as it would make testing a bit faster, but if this takes too much work than it's worth, than opening a new one is fine for now.
